NITI Aayog organises National Workshop on SDG Budgeting in Kolkata under the State Support Mission, in collaboration with the Government of West Bengal and UNDP
articles.full_content:
NITI Aayog, in collaboration with the Government of West Bengal and with technical support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), organised a National Workshop on SDG Budgeting in Kolkata on 29 September 2026 under the State Support Mission (SSM) initiative of NITI Aayog. The Workshop focused on strengthening the alignment of planning and budgeting processes with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), with emphasis on institutionalising SDG budget tagging and translating financial commitments into measurable development outcomes at the sub-national level.
The Workshop brought together participants from 32 States and Union Territories, along with senior officials from NITI Aayog, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) and its offices, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Controller General of Accounts (CGA), Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), UNDP, UN Resident Coordinator Office (UNRCO), development partners, and representatives from FICCI, CII, SEBI, Tata Steel Foundation, Intellecap and GIZ. Government representatives from Haryana, Odisha, Meghalaya and West Bengal shared experiences on the implementation and institutionalisation of SDG Budgeting, reflecting the whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to SDG localisation.
The inaugural session was graced by Dr. Swapan Dasgupta, Hon'ble Finance Minister, Government of West Bengal; Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Hon'ble Member, NITI Aayog; Shri K. Sanjay Murthy, Comptroller and Auditor General of India, virtually; Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser, Government of India, virtually; Shri Prabhat Kumar Mishra, Additional Chief Secretary, Finance, Government of West Bengal; Shri Stefan Priesner, United Nations Resident Coordinator; Dr. Angela Lusigi, Resident Representative, UNDP; and Shri Rajib Kumar Sen, Programme Director (SDGs), NITI Aayog.
Delivering the Chief Guest Address, Dr. Swapan Dasgupta said, "What we have not always had is a clean line running from a goal, to a target, to an allocation in the budget, to a unit that will actually spend. Without that line, the SDGs remain an aspiration on the asset side of the ledger with no corresponding entry on the liability side. SDG budget tagging is the discipline of drawing that line."
In his keynote address, Dr. R. Balasubramaniam said, "Mapping the SDGs to State expenditure is a significant step. Whole-of-society and whole-of-government can sound like slogans, but with the finance department, political leadership, multilateral institutions and the private sector together today, the idea becomes real. The task ahead is to guide every State so that money spent can be shown to be money spent wisely”.

MoEFCC Commences Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 to Institutionalize Swachhata, Minimize Pendency and Promote Scientific E-Waste Management
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) today commenced the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 , being observed from 02.10.2026 to 31.10.2026 , with the objectives of institutionalizing Swachhata and minimizing pendency in Government offices. The Campaign is being undertaken across the Ministry, including its Subordinate Offices, Autonomous Organisations, Regional Offices and other field and outstation offices, with particular emphasis on offices having public interface or providing public services.
Special Campaign 6 is being undertaken in accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). This year's Campaign focuses on “Effective Collection, Segregation and Disposal of E-Waste” , along with cleanliness of campaign sites, disposal of pending matters, records management, space management, process simplification and disposal of redundant items and furniture.
The Ministry has also communicated the Campaign guidelines and the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for scientific disposal of e-waste to all its Organisations and Offices.
As part of the Preparatory Phase, MoEFCC has identified targets under various parameters, including cleanliness, pendency liquidation and record management. The targets include
Target identified
Cleanliness Campaign Sites
References from Members of Parliament
Parliamentary Assurances
Inter-Ministerial/Cabinet References
State Government References
Public Grievances
Public Grievance Appeals
Physical Files identified for Review
E-Files identified for Review
Information Technology and Telecommunication Equipment
Consumer Electrical and Electronics and Photovoltaic Panels
Large and Small Electrical and Electronic Equipment
Electrical and Electronic Tools
Toys, Leisure and Sports Equipment
Laboratory Instruments
The e-waste identified by the Organisations and Offices will be processed in accordance with the applicable Rules and the SOP guidelines finalized by DARPG.
The Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6 has also commenced in all Subordinate Offices, Autonomous Organisations and Regional Offices. Nodal Officers have been designated to coordinate and monitor the activities, ensure timely reporting and facilitate achievement of the identified targets. The Ministry will continue to monitor progress through the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) Portal of DARPG , which will be updated regularly during this Phase.

The Campaign is being undertaken across the Ministry, including its Subordinate Offices, Autonomous Organisations, Regional Offices and other field and outstation offices, with particular emphasis on offices having public interface or providing public services. Special Campaign 6 is being undertaken in accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG).

Shri Narendra Bhooshan assumes charge as Secretary of Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
articles.full_content:
Shri Narendra Bhooshan, a 1992-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Uttar Pradesh cadre, has assumed charge as Secretary of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India.
Shri Bhooshan brings with him over three decades of administrative experience across the Central and State Governments, with wide exposure to energy, infrastructure, industry, agriculture, urban development, finance and land-resource management. His appointment as Secretary, MoEFCC follows his tenure as Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development.
Career Background
During his career in the Uttar Pradesh cadre, Shri Bhooshan has held several senior assignments, including Additional Chief Secretary, Energy and Additional Energy Source and Technical Education. Earlier he served as Principal Secretary in the departments of PWD, Infrastructure and Industries Development, I.T. and Electronics, Science and Technology, Panchayati Raj. He has also served as Chief Executive Officer, Greater Noida Authority, besides holding other important charges. Shri Bhooshan also carries substantial field experience, having served as the District Magistrate of Mathura, Firozabad, and Udham Singh Nagar.
At the Government of India level, Shri Bhooshan has served as Deputy Director General, Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), Mission Director, National Food Security Management, and Joint Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Cooperation. He has also served as Officer on Special Duty in the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
Shri Bhooshan holds a graduate degree in Electronics and a Master's degree in International Development Policy from Duke University, USA. His professional training includes programmes relating to public finance, infrastructure and climate-change preparedness.

Shri Bhooshan brings with him over three decades of administrative experience across the Central and State Governments, with wide exposure to energy, infrastructure, industry, agriculture, urban development, finance and land-resource management. His appointment as Secretary, MoEFCC follows his tenure as Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development.

Hindi Fortnight-2026 Concluded at the Regional Office of the Employees' State Insurance Corporation, Haryana
articles.full_content:
In a Hindi-speaking state like Haryana, it is our responsibility to perform all work in Hindi – Mr. Hari Om Prakash, Regional Director
The conclusion of the Hindi Fortnight, which was ongoing since September 14 at the Regional Office of the Employees' State Insurance Corporation, Ministry of Labour and Employment, was marked by a prize distribution ceremony honoring the winners of various competitions held during the fortnight. Officers and employees actively participated in this grand event, during which the appeal made by the Director General, ESIC, urging all official work to be transacted in Hindi, was read out to the gathered assembly.
Presiding over the function, Shri Hari Om Prakash, Regional Director, Haryana, stated that in Haryana, a Hindi-speaking region, it is the collective duty of all staff to execute all official work in Hindi itself. He emphasized that this approach enables the organization to reach the worker standing at the last mile who lacks awareness regarding the various benefits provided by the Employees' State Insurance Corporation.
During the ceremony, Private Secretary Ms. Meena Verma and Assistant Ms. Manisha Kalra recited spirited poems, which were greatly appreciated by the attending personnel. Under the Hindi Fortnight, competitions for Essay Writing, Noting and Drafting, Official Language Knowledge, and Elocution were organized, and the successful participants were honored with mementos and certificates.
For the valedictory event, the entire office was decorated with floral patterns (rangoli) and garlands by the female staff, filling the atmosphere of the office with beauty and fragrance.
On this occasion, the Coordination Branch was awarded the Hindi Running Shield for demonstrating the best official Hindi implementation throughout the year. The ceremony was attended by Deputy Directors Shri Shiv Shakti Sharma, Shri Vivekanand, Shri Vivek, Smt. Poonam Bala, and Shri Brijesh Mishra, Assistant Director (Official Language), along with other officers and employees.

articles.full_content:
Dr Virendra Kumar To Lead ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ Tree Plantation Drive Under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign
As part of the Central Government’s continued commitment towards the welfare and dignity of senior citizens, Dr. Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, will distribute assistive devices among senior citizens at a programme at Dr Ambedkar International Centre in National Capital here tomorrow. Shri B. L. Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment, will also grace the occasion.
A Senior Official in the Ministry informed that under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY), 114 senior citizens residing in Senior Citizens’ Homes in New Delhi and the National Capital Region will receive a total of 662 assistive devices and aids costing over ₹10 lakh, free of cost. The devices have been identified according to the individual needs of the beneficiaries through assessment camps conducted in September 2026.
The assistive devices include folding wheelchairs and commode wheelchairs, crutches, walking sticks, BTE hearing aids, spinal supports, walkers, cervical collars, chairs with commode, knee braces, LS belts, tripods/tetrapods and silicone foam cushions.
The initiative reflects the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment’s continued commitment to enabling senior citizens to live with dignity, good health and independence.
The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment is the nodal department for the welfare of senior citizens in the country. Its Senior Citizens Division formulates and implements policies and programmes for the elderly in close collaboration with State Governments, Non-Governmental Organisations and civil society. The Division administers the umbrella scheme Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), and the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana is a key component.
The Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana is implemented by the Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO), a Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The distribution of assistive devices is in consonance with the Government’s vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, which seeks to ensure inclusive growth and enable every citizen, including senior citizens, to live with dignity, good health and independence.
Under the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign , a tree sapling plantation drive with the theme “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” will be led by Dr. Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, tomorrow on the occasion of Swachh Bharat Diwas. The plantation drive is scheduled to be held at Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation in New Delhi. The initiative will reinforce the message of environmental sustainability, cleanliness and collective responsibility, while encouraging citizens to contribute towards a greener, cleaner and healthier India.

Goa Steps Up Implementation of Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 with Four-Way Segregation and Stronger Compliance
articles.full_content:
412 Bulk Waste Generators identified and registered; fortnightly inspections, 14 RRR Centres and citizen grievance redressal strengthened
Goa, 1 October 2026
The Department of Municipal Administration, Directorate of Panchayats, Press Information Bureau and Goa State Pollution Control Board jointly organised a Regional Press Conference on the implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 at the Conference Hall, Central Library, Panaji, today.
The press conference was attended by Shri Brijesh Manerkar, Director of Urban Development; Dr Geeta Nagvenkar, Member Secretary, Goa State Pollution Control Board; Shri Dashrath Redkar, Director of Panchayats; and Shri Nana Meshram, Director, PIB.
Shri Brijesh Manerkar, highlighted various measures being undertaken in Urban Local Bodies of Goa for effective implementation of the Rules and compliance with the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court dated 5 May 2026.
He further stated The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, notified by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, came into effect from 1 April 2026, replacing the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016. The new Rules emphasise source segregation, scientific waste management, Circular Economy, Extended Producer Responsibility and the Polluter Pays principle.
He also stated A key focus of implementation in Goa is four-way segregation of waste at source into Green: Wet and biodegradable waste, Blue: Dry and recyclable waste, Red: Sanitary waste and Black: Special-care waste, including batteries, expired medicines, CFLs and other notified materials requiring special handling.
Shri Manerkar stressed that The Councillor /Mayors and their Chairpersons, Corporator, or Sarpanch/Panch/ Ward Member, being the primary elected representative of the people,are designated as the lead facilitators for source-segregation education. It is their statutory duty to engage every citizen within their ward in the implementation of the 2026 Rules.
He also said that The Government is continues promoting segregation through awareness, IEC and behavioural-change activities involving households, institutions, businesses and other waste generators across the state.
Shri Manerkar said that Bulk Waste Generators (BWGs) are being brought under a structured registration and compliance framework. Establishments meeting prescribed thresholds, including 20,000 sq. metres or more of floor area, 40,000 litres of daily water consumption or generation of 100 kg or more of solid waste per day, fall within the BWG criteria. As on 30 September 2026, 412 BWGs had been identified across Goa — 195 in North Goa, 202 in South Goa and 15 in Kushavati — and the material presented at the conference states that all identified BWGs had been registered on the CPCB portal.

NSO Launches October 2026 Survey Drive, Appeals to Citizens and Enterprises for Cooperation
articles.full_content:
The Field Operations Division of National Statistics Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India is engaged in collecting information from households and establishments since 1950 which is used for planning and policy formulation both at National and State level.
Information is collected by trained officers of the NSO using hand-held digital devices (tablets) equipped with e-Sigma software and secure web portals designated for enterprise surveys. All information collected in these surveys is kept strictly confidential. The identity of households and enterprises participating in the survey is not disclosed in any report or published data. The data is used only for statistical purposes.
The detail of surveys undertaken by NSO (FOD) during the month of October, 2026 in various Districts is attached as Annexure-I. Further, for Wholesale Price Index, Purchaser Price Index, Index of Industrial Production and Annual Survey of Incorporated Service Sector Enterprises, selected units have been sent notices and are contacted by NSO (FOD) officials for data collection time to time. The Government, therefore, requests all the citizens/enterprise mentioned in Annexure-I to kindly extend full cooperation to the survey officials and spare valuable time to provide correct and complete information. Participation from all the citizens helps in better planning and development for the benefit of the nation.

articles.full_content:
It was an eventful and action-oriented day at the Ministry of Coal as a series of activities were organised today under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 and Special Campaign 6, bringing together the themes of cleanliness, environmental responsibility and community welfare. Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, Secretary, Ministry of Coal, Ministry of Coal, and Shri Sanoj Kumar Jha, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Coal, Smt. Rupinder Brar, Additional Secretary along with senior officers and officials of the Ministry, participated in the activities.

Senior officers and officials actively participated in the drive, reinforcing the message that cleanliness is a collective responsibility and requires sustained participation.
Adding a humanitarian dimension to the day’s activities, a Blood Donation Camp was organised near the Entry Gate of GPOA-3. Officers and officials participated in the camp and contributed towards the noble cause of blood donation, reflecting the spirit of compassion, community service and social responsibility.
The active participation of the Ministry’s senior leadership, officers and officials gave further impetus to the objectives of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 and Special Campaign 6. The initiatives brought together environmental awareness, cleanliness and community welfare, translating the spirit of collective responsibility into meaningful action.
The day’s activities reflected the spirit of collective participation and responsible citizenship, with officers and officials coming together to contribute towards cleanliness, environmental sustainability and community welfare. Centre of Excellence on Green Hydrogen inaugurated at Jadavpur University
articles.full_content:
Kolkata, October 1, 2026
The Centre of Excellence on Green Hydrogen (CoE GH2) was inaugurated today at Jadavpur University, Kolkata as a part of the National Green Hydrogen Mission of the Union Ministry of New & Renewable Energy. Shri Rajesh Pandey, Chairman, Damodar Valley Corporation, graced the occasion as Chief Guest of the function and inaugurated the Centre of Excellence. The distinguished dignitaries present included Professor Dr. Chiranjib Bhattacharjee, Vice Chancellor, Jadavpur University, Shri Swapnendu Kumar Panda, Member (Technical), DVC and Professor Amitava Datta, pro-Vice Chancellor, JU.
The Centre came into being as a joint initiative of DVC, Jadavpur University, Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) and Hindustan Urvarak & Rasayan Limited (HURL), supported and funded by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) and DVC. Jadavpur University is the knowledge partner, while SAIL and HURL are industry stakeholders. Mr. Arghyajit Saha, General Manager, Environment Management Division, SAIL was present as industry partner.
Selected through a nationwide process, it is one of only four such Centres pan-India approved under the National Green Hydrogen Mission of the Ministry of New & Renewable Energy,GoI which aims to make India a global hub for the production, use and export of green hydrogen.
The Centre will focus on high-pressure compression, storage and transportation of green hydrogen, and on its applications in decarbonising the power, steel and fertiliser sectors. It is expected to deliver stable and efficient green hydrogen co-firing burner systems, efficient high-pressure compression, and cleaner steel and fertiliser production, contributing to India’s clean energy transition.

articles.full_content:
The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has shared an article written by Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat.
The article highlights India’s rise on the global tourism map, supported by better connectivity, improved tourist facilities and easier digital access. It notes that this growth is opening new opportunities for local businesses, guides, artisans and communities.
The article further highlights sustainability as a key focus for the next phase of tourism, connecting India’s rich heritage with economic opportunity while creating better experiences for travellers.
The Prime Minister’s Office said in X post;
“India’s rise on the global tourism map reflects better connectivity, improved tourist facilities and easier digital access, writes Union Minister @gssjodhpur. This growth is opening new opportunities for local businesses, guides, artisans and communities.
With sustainability at the heart of tourism’s next phase, India is connecting its rich heritage with economic opportunity as well as creating better experiences for travellers.”

articles.full_content:
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) celebrates its Tenth Annual Day
Minister of State for Corporate Affairs Ministry and Road Transport and Highways, Shri Harsh Malhotra inaugurated the 10th Annual Day celebrations of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi today, marking ten years of IBBI since its establishment on 1st October, 2016.
Chief guest Shri Harsh Malhotra in his inaugural address, observed that the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) has strengthened credit discipline, improved the recovery climate and contributed to the ease of doing business in the country. He noted the Government’s commitment to keep the Code responsive to emerging needs, including through the recent legislative amendments, and urged all stakeholders to work towards faster and value-maximising resolutions in the decade ahead.
MoS Shri Malhotra highlighted the need for improved adoption of emerging technologies, including AI, in IBC ecosystem. He noted that the efforts should be made towards faster resolutions and value maximisation as way forward.
Justice Shri Anupinder Singh Grewal, Hon’ble President, National Company Law Tribunal, reflected to the role of the Adjudicating Authority in the IBC framework. He highlighted the steps being taken to reduce delays in disposal of cases and recent improvements in speedier disposal of resolution plans. He noted various areas of reforms that may be considered in coming times including revision in admission thresholds, use of mediation, sector specific carveouts, etc.
Shri Indevar Pandey, Hon’ble Member, National Company Law Appellate Tribunal shared his perspective on the evolution of insolvency jurisprudence over the decade and the issues that may be considered in coming times. He highlighted that the IBC has seen seven sets of amendments to the Code in the last ten years. While noting the constraints involved in amending laws, he appreciated that amendments to the Code and regulations are being carried out in line with emerging needs in a timely manner. While noting the positive outcomes of IBC, he emphasised the need for timelines to be respected by all stakeholders.
Shri Ansuman Pattnaik, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, while noting the achievements of the IBC, highlighted the policy reforms undertaken to strengthen the Code, including the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2026. He noted key aspects of the amendment act and outlined the areas for the next phase of reforms in IBC framework and ecosystem.
Welcoming the guests, Shri Jayanti Prasad, Chairperson, IBBI, reflected on the ten-year journey of the Code and the Board. He noted that IBC has enabled substantial recoveries for creditors, rescued viable businesses across sectors, and brought about a lasting change in
